capabilities: Sync vault notes across devices through a self-hosted Postgres database fronted by PostgREST
Embed every note into a pgvector column via a llama.cpp-compatible embedding server
Query the embedded notes as a semantic search index from outside Obsidian
Pull remote changes and reconcile local notes on startup or on demand
Apply SQL schema and version migrations to the backend database
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README warns that HTTP exposes note content and API keys in transit, that PostgREST's max-rows must not be set below 100, and that the 0.1.1 migration needs a maintenance window because it can block reads and writes. Sync is last-write-wins with no conflict resolution and is not built for real-time collaboration.
intentEvidence: instead of Obsidian Sync, iCloud, or a CouchDB setup
problem: Obsidian's built-in sync options are a paid service or a CouchDB setup, and neither leaves you with a queryable embedding index of your notes.
